version** 1.2 (but also tested with 1.0) **Bug description** Reprojecting a map in ICRS coordinates of given spatial binning gives weird binning patterns when reprojecting to another ICRS geometry when _preserve_counts = true_, depending on the binning. For our input binning of 0.1 deg per axis, reprojected pixel sizes of 0.05 deg or 0.025 deg work fine, whereas 0.06 deg (larger, so not really precision-factor-related) or 0.02 deg are problematic. **To Reproduce** See example code with example input map. **Other information** We’ve traced the issue to its origin; within reproject_to_geom the issue is caused by the input_map.resample call, and within this function it further points to the _resample_by_idx function. In our case that one is defined in /maps/wcs/ndmap.py. Here we discovered that the crucial part is the division of the weights by np.bincount in the if not preserve_counts call. And indeed, when setting preserve_counts to false the weird pattern does not appear (see test code). So it seems that the previous call weights = np.bincount(…) causes an uneven distribution of original bins in the weights within the final geometry, which needs to be corrected for by this division regardless if preserve_counts is true or false. In case preserve_counts is true, a subsequently applied scaling factor would probably do the trick; however it’s probably best if one of the core developers would have a look and check what the best way is (especially what this normalization factor should exactly be). +    def run(self, datasets):

+            )
+        
+        result = self._sampler.run(min_num_live_points=self.min_num_live_points, frac_remain=self.frac_remain)
+        
+        return result

+    one degree of freedom per valid energy bin in each dataset.
+    This method implemented here is valid under the assumption

+    then the sum of the TS also follows a Chi2 distribution (with the sum of degree of freedom).
+
+    See, Zhen (2014): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167947313003204,

+

+    dataset : `~gammapy.datasets.Datasets`
+        Datasets containing only `~gammapy.datasets.MapDataset`.
+
+    Returns

+    results : dict
+        Dictionary with entries:
+

+                * "df" : degree of freedom map (one norm per valid bin).
+                * "npred_excess" : summed excess map.
+                * "estimator_results" : dictionary containing the flux maps computed for each dataset.

+

+

This pull request fixes two small bugs that are preventing `gammapy.data.ObservationsEventsSampler` to work on full-enclosure-based observations (for the point-like case see #5544 ).

I can add a new tutorial with a short snippet on how to use this class (either as a separate PR after this fix PR is merged or directly here if preferred by the maintainers).

Regarding the testing (to be integrated):
- the fix for `dataset_kwargs` is needed because in the test this is always defined, never `None`
- the energy axes fix is needed because of the fix above (if the axis is None when `create_map_dataset_from_observation` is called then the (faulty) function `_default_energy_axis` is called

Closes #5542.

This pull request fixes two small bugs that are preventing `gammapy.data.ObservationsEventsSampler` to work on full-enclosure-based observations (for the point-like case see #5544 ).

I can add a new tutorial with a short snippet on how to use this class (either as a separate PR after this fix PR is merged or directly here if preferred by the maintainers).

Regarding the testing (to be integrated):
- the fix for `dataset_kwargs` is needed because in the test this is always defined, never `None`
- the energy axes fix is needed because of the fix above (if the axis is None when `create_map_dataset_from_observation` is called then the (faulty) function `_default_energy_axis` is called

Closes #5542.

> I think we should avoid solutions where different behavior are applied at the data handling and makers level. I would rather put the patch at the irf IO level e.g. reverting fov_lon axis in `Background.read`. In general, future versions of data format might have different conventions. We have to clarify the internal gammapy convention and stick to it. The IRF objects we use should follow these conventions independently of their initial format.

It cannot be done in in `Background.read` because the necessary meta key are not on the background header.

Current master

**Bug description**

In `gammapy/utils/coordinates/fov`, `sky_to_fov` is defined like this:

```python
    # Create a frame that is centered on the pointing position
    center = SkyCoord(lon_pnt, lat_pnt)
    fov_frame = SkyOffsetFrame(origin=center)

    # Define coordinate to be transformed.
    target_sky = SkyCoord(lon, lat)

    # Transform into FoV-system
    target_fov = target_sky.transform_to(fov_frame)

    # Switch sign of longitude angle since this axis is
    # reversed in our definition of the FoV-system
    return -target_fov.lon, target_fov.lat

```

Observe the `-` in front of `target_fov.lon`.

The only place this function is used is in `gammapy/makers/utils.py`, where there is an if condition and the same transformation is basically done "by hand" again: 

https://github.com/gammapy/gammapy/blob/a3f6b0945b15cfea1d5fc3f711ef58929161d49a/gammapy/makers/utils.py#L60-L89


But this time, no `-` in front of `lon`.

This seems inconsistent. Is this a bug? Or intentional? Then there should proabbly be some kind of comment why it is negated in the one function but not in the "by hand" approach, which essentially duplicates the same code again.

v1.2 there was a large effort made to fix the formatting of docstrings. We did not keep an eye on this as we introduced new functionality throughout the past 8 months. 
Therefore I think it is useful to include in the documentation how to check the docstrings with pydocstyle. We should all be using this before we push a PR so that they are in the correct format

Another thing I added was how to handle bullet points in the docstrings. This is often done incorrectly and therefore not rendered correctly in the docs. +def get_combined_flux_maps(

+    method="gaussian_errors",
+    reference_model=None,
+    dnde_scan_axis=None,
+):
+    """Create a FluxMaps by combining a list of flux maps with the same geometry.
+
+     This assumes the flux maps are independent measurements of the same true value.
+     The GTI is stacked in the process.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    estimator : `~gammapy.estimators.ExcessMapEstimator` or `~gammapy.estimators.TSMapEstimator`
+        Excess Map Estimator or TS Map Estimator
+    dataset : `~gammapy.datasets.Datasets`
+        Datasets containing only `~gammapy.datasets.MapDataset`.
+    method : {"gaussian_errors"}
+        * gaussian_errors :
+            Under the gaussian error approximation the likelihood is given by the gaussian distibution.
+            The product of gaussians is also a gaussian so can derive dnde, dnde_err, and ts.
+        * distrib :
+            Likelihood profile approximation assuming that probabilities distributions for
+            flux points correspond to asymmetric gaussians and for upper limits to complementary error functions.
+            Use available quantities among dnde, dnde_err, dnde_errp, dnde_errn, dnde_ul, and ts.
+        * profile :
+            Sum the likelihood profile maps.
+            The flux maps must contains the `stat_scan` maps.
+
+        Default is "gaussian_errors" which is the faster but least accurate solution,
+        "distrib"  will be more accurate if dnde_errp and dnde_errn are available,
+        "profile"  will be even more accurate if "stat_scan" is available.
+
+    reference_model : `~gammapy.modeling.models.SkyModel`, optional
+        Reference model to use for conversions.
+        Default is None and is will use the reference_model of the first FluxMaps in the list.
+
+    dnde_scan_axis : `~gammapy.maps.MapAxis`
+        Map axis providing the dnde values used to compute the profile.
+        Default is None and it will be derived from the first FluxMaps in the list.
+        Used only if `method` is distrib or profile.
+
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    results : dict
+        Dictionary with entries:
+
+                * "flux_maps" : `~gammapy.estimators.FluxMaps`
+                * "estimator_results" : dictionary containing the estimator results for each version**
1.2

**Bug description**
When initializing a `TemplateSpatialModel`, there is no check for `nan` values in the input map. In case `normalize=True` (the default), this will result in a map attached to the model that is `nan` in all pixels, as the normalization involves a sum over all pixels, which is `nan` if there is a single pixel with `nan` entry.

**Expected behavior**
I see two solutions here: either a warning should be issued if any of the pixels in the input map has a `nan` entry (such a warning already exists e.g. for negative pixels), or pixels with `nan` entries should be ignored in the normalization (i.e. use `np.nansum` [here](https://github.com/gammapy/gammapy/blob/ba580c7926a7e5bd44e2933323f11d8b370660d6/gammapy/modeling/models/spatial.py#L1321) and [here](https://github.com/gammapy/gammapy/blob/ba580c7926a7e5bd44e2933323f11d8b370660d6/gammapy/modeling/models/spatial.py#L1324)). I think I would prefer the second option (at least I see nothing wrong per se with `nan` values in the map).

I'm happy to help with fixing this, but would like to hear some opinions about the preferred solution first.","reactions":{"url":"https://api.github.com/repos/gammapy/gammapy/issues/5379/reactions","total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"hooray":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"timeline_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/gammapy/gammapy/issues/5379/timeline","performed_via_github_app":null,"state_reason":"completed"}}
